## Highlights

- When an agent's workspace has reached its limit of four concurrent executions, a new run
  waits for a place instead of failing. Finishing a run wakes the oldest waiter in that
  workspace; waiting does not consume an automatic retry.
  [Task automation](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/task-automation)
  · [#4481](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4481)
- Coding agents can discover their granted workspace tools even when they call
  `workspace_status` through the `workspace_tool` wrapper. The bridge routes that exact
  discovery call to the existing status endpoint. Tool permissions and session authentication
  still apply; an agent does not gain a tool by discovering it.
  [#4496](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4496)
- An agent that implemented a task cannot delegate the review of its own result, even if it has
  the review-delegation permission. An independent manager can still hand the captured review
  to an eligible reviewer through the existing guarded workflow.
  [Review delegation](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/projects/task-automation#delegate-review)
  · [#4487](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4487)
- **Message information** shows the model and provider used for a reply, token usage and timing,
  and the serving provider, region or specific model version when that information is available.
  An unreported region stays **Not reported** rather than being inferred from a provider's name.
  [Reply details](https://docs.tale.dev/platform/chat/basics#reply-details)
  · [#4493](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4493)
- Operators can collect a fresh managed-deployment acceptance receipt with `tale deploy accept`.
  It checks the completed deployment, running images and migration ledgers, and verifies that
  the canonical HTTPS origin reaches the frontend and API processes observed locally. A
  different installation running the same version is refused.
  [CLI install](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/install/cli-install#verify-the-current-deployment)
  · [#4492](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4492)
  · [#4497](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4497)
- German and French interface wording follows the existing product labels more consistently,
  including **Arbeitsbereich**, **Inhaber** and **Conservation légale**. The German website's
  navigation, page eyebrows and product demos use **Agenten** and **Richtlinien**; some page titles
  and text still say Agents and Governance
  ([#4483](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4483)). Stored settings and translation keys
  are unchanged.
  [#4489](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4489)
  · [#4490](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4490)

## Upgrade notes

- Back up the application and knowledge databases, configuration, keys and external stores
  before deploying. Relative to v0.5.76, this release adds no database migration, operator
  environment variable or Compose service. When upgrading from an earlier version, retain the
  [v0.5.76 upgrade requirements](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/blob/v0.5.76/.github/release-notes/v0.5.76.md),
  including the ordered knowledge-corpus migrations and the prior-release requirements linked
  there.
- Deploy the matching platform, sandbox spawner and sandbox-runtime images to receive the
  workspace-capacity and tool-discovery repairs. The platform, web, docs, UI docs, AI gateway and
  sandbox images now run Bun 1.4.2 instead of 1.3.12, and the sandbox runtime's `bun` is pinned to
  1.4.2 as well. The runtime upgrade uses a full deployment; a configuration-only update cannot
  install these changes. Existing tool and secret grants are preserved.
  [#4486](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4486)
- Use this release's CLI and compatible runtime for deployment acceptance. Prepare the bundle
  with its full deployment source reference and complete the normal deployment first. Older
  bundles remain deployable, but cannot provide the new acceptance proof without the
  source-derived migration inventory and compatible serving processes. Acceptance requires
  the bundle, full CLI and deployment source commits, and the independently selected version
  without the `v` prefix. It observes state at that time; it does not promise that routing or
  processes remain unchanged later.
- Acceptance does not apply configuration, restart services or run migrations. It takes the
  deployment lock and creates and removes a private temporary bundle copy. Docker and HTTPS
  observations share a 120-second budget. Preparation elapsed time counts toward that budget,
  but filesystem copy and cleanup cannot be interrupted by it. Use an external process
  supervisor when a whole-command deadline is required. The public serving-process identities
  are correlation data, not credentials. They arrive in a new `Tale-Serving-Identity` response
  header on Tale's health endpoints, including the frontend's `/api/health` and the API's
  `/api/health/ready`, so a proxy in front of Tale must pass it through; the JSON bodies are
  unchanged.
  [Acceptance requirements](https://docs.tale.dev/self-hosted/install/cli-install#verify-the-current-deployment)
- The release candidate source contract (`.github/release-candidate-contract.json`) adds backend
  integration's **Verify current deployment acceptance ledgers** step. An adopter that pins the
  contract's digest must review the new digest before adopting this release.
  [#4492](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4492)
- If you grant `task_delegate_review`, deploy this release first: v0.5.76 accepts a delegation
  from the implementation agent of the reviewed work.
  [#4487](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4487)
- Known issues carried into this release include the projects overview's older **Environment**
  wording ([#4454](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/issues/4454)). For replies that call tools,
  the timing breakdown can include tool execution within model phases; do not treat those
  phases or output speed as isolated model benchmarks.
  [#4498](https://github.com/tale-project/tale/pull/4498)
